#The content blocker

Wren blocks advertising, tracking and malware natively: the filter engine (src/adblock) is a portable Odin package, the policy layer (src/blocker) joins it to the loader and the pages, and the interface is native (the shield at the end of the address bar, its panel, and the dashboard about:blocker). Nothing is ever reported anywhere; the lists are downloaded from their own servers, never shipped in the repository (the only list built in is a small one written for Wren).

The motivation is performance: a blocked request costs no DNS lookup, no connection, no script to download, parse and run, and its frame or image leaves no empty box. Measurements are at the end.

#Architecture

 lists (text) --compile--> index (one binary blob) --load--> adblock.Engine --match--> Verdict
   downloaded in the background        cached in the profile        read-only, no allocation per request
   (conditional requests, checked)     (loaded in ~13 ms)
                                                    ^
 fetch.Loader --Interceptor--> blocker (counts, journal, dynamic rules, site switches) ----+
 page --embedder hooks--> element hiding before the first paint, procedural selectors, scriptlets

#src/adblock: the engine (independent, an API an extension API can sit on)

callwhat it does
compile(lists, env, include) / Builderparses the lists (ABP, uBlock Origin and AdGuard syntax, hosts files, !#if / !#include) and builds the index blob
engine_load(blob, own, verify)reads a blob in place (checked by a checksum), builds the bloom filters
match(engine, &request)Verdict: Allow, Block, Redirect (with the stand-in's name) or Exception, and the filter that decided
rewrite_url, csp_directives, match_response_headers$removeparam, $csp, $header
page_flags(engine, url)$document, $elemhide, $generichide, $specifichide exceptions of a page
cosmetic_for_host, cosmetic_keyedelement hiding, scriptlets and HTML filters of a host, with exceptions applied; the generic selectors keyed to a class or id
filter_ref, line_at, validate_listwhere a filter came from (list and offset) and the line to show, the validity of a downloaded list

The index is one 8-byte aligned blob: string pool, 28-byte filter records, domain lists, and per class (block, allow, redirect, removeparam, csp, header, page) a table by request host, a table by token, a table of 4-byte windows for filters without a token, a table by source domain and a short always-checked list. Candidate lists carry the type and party bits of each filter, so most candidates are discarded without reading their record. Regular expressions run on a Pike VM (linear time, no catastrophic backtracking) behind an ordered list of required literals. Text of the rules is not stored: a filter remembers (list, offset), and the journal reads the line from the .src file written with the index.

#src/blocker: the policy layer

  • fetch.Interceptor (src/fetch/intercept.odin): called before DNS and connection, at the first hop and after each redirect, for documents, frames, scripts, styles, images, fonts, media, fetch / XHR, beacons, WebSocket handshakes and workers' requests; and with the response headers. It can block (error net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT, reported to the DevTools observer with Observed.blocked_by naming the rule), answer with a stand-in ($redirect), rewrite the URL ($removeparam), add a Content-Security-Policy ($csp) or block on a header ($header, large media).
  • Dynamic rules (the matrix) are evaluated first and win over the lists; then the per-site switches (hard mode, remote fonts); then the engine.
  • Per tab: counters, a time series of the blocks (the panel's graph), the hosts the page talked to by request type.
  • Lists: CATALOG (uBlock filters family, EasyList, EasyPrivacy, AdGuard, Peter Lowe's list, URLhaus, regional and annoyance lists), custom lists by URL. A round downloads what is due (blocker.update.interval_hours), one list at a time, with If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since; a body that is not a filter list is refused and the previous copy stays; compilation runs on a thread named wren-blocker-compile at below-normal priority and the loop thread swaps the engine (documents keep the engine their cosmetic result came from until they end).
  • HTML filters (html_filter.odin): the ##^ filters of the visited host are applied to the body of its document (and frame) response, on the loader, before the parser reads it (rewrite_filter, a fetch.Body_Filter). The whole HTML body is held (up to blocker.html_filters.max_body, past which it streams through untouched), scanned with a tolerant byte parser (no DOM: tag delimiters, nesting of the same tag, the raw text of <script> / <style> / <textarea> / <title>), and every element a rule matches is deleted by byte range. The bytes are left in their original charset (only byte ranges are removed; nothing is re-encoded); :has-text decodes just the matched element's text to UTF-8 for the comparison. HTML answers of the targeted host only (never other types); the #@#^ exceptions switch the host off; each removal is counted and logged (outcome "element removed (HTML filter)").
  • Popups (popup.odin): the $popup filters stop the pop-up windows and tabs a page opens. The page's window.open path asks the blocker (page.embedder.popup_check) with the opener document and the target URL; a $popup match blocks the opening (no tab is created), exceptions (@@||x^$popup, $~popup) win. A pop-up backed by a recent click or key press (HTML transient activation) to the opener's own registrable domain is never stopped; one a script opens on its own is. Counted and logged (outcome "popup blocked").
  • Pages (page_hooks.odin, procedural.odin, scriptlets.js): the cosmetic filters of the host become a user-origin stylesheet before the first style computation; generic .class / #id selectors are applied only when the DOM has that class or id (looked up again, debounced, when the DOM changes); procedural selectors are evaluated natively on the DOM and hide through the style engine (nothing is added to the page); scriptlets are carried out by the route that costs the page least (next section): on the DOM, on the response, or as hooks of the engine. Blocked frames and images are hidden.

#Syntax understood

Network: ||host^, |, *, ^, /regex/; $third-party (3p, 1p, first-party), the types script image stylesheet xmlhttprequest subdocument media font websocket ping object other document popup webrtc csp_report, all; $domain= (from=), $to=, $denyallow=, $method=, $important, $match-case, $badfilter, $redirect=, $redirect-rule=, $rewrite=abp-resource:, $empty, $mp4, $removeparam= (name or /regex/), $csp=, $inline-script, $inline-font, $header=, $replace=/search/replacement/flags (the response text, any type), $generichide, $elemhide, $specifichide; exceptions @@. A line with an option the engine does not know ($cookie=, $ipaddress=...) is not a filter: it is counted as "not understood", as uBlock Origin does, and the dashboard shows the lines (My filters) and the count per list (Statistics).

Cosmetic: ##, #@#, entities (google.*), ~domain exclusions; procedural :has() :has-text() :contains() :-abp-contains() :-abp-has() :matches-css() :matches-attr() :matches-path() :min-text-length() :not() :upward() :nth-ancestor() :remove() :style(); AdGuard #$# style injections and #%#//scriptlet(); ##+js(name, args...).

HTML filters: ##^selector (and the exceptions #@#^) remove elements from a document's markup before it is parsed, so an inline ad script or a tracker iframe never exists (not hidden — gone). The selector is one element with script iframe div * ^script (a tag name, *, or uBlock's leading ^), [attr] [attr=v] [attr*=v] [attr^=v] [attr$=v] [attr~=v], :has-text(x) / :contains(x) (plain, * glob or /regex/), and :not(:has-text(x)) / :not([attr]). Examples: example.com##^script:has-text(window.adConfig), example.com##^iframe[src*="/ads/"].

#Scriptlets: where each one is carried out

The blocker does not run JavaScript in a page when it can do the thing natively. Each scriptlet (uBlock Origin's names, aliases and .js suffixes; scriptlet_route.odin) has a route, from the cheapest for the page:

routescriptletshow
DOM (Odin, no realm)remove-attr (ra), remove-class (rc), set-attr (sa), remove-node-text (rmnt), replace-node-text (rpnt, trusted-replace-node-text), click-element (trusted-click-element), href-sanitizer, disable-newtab-links, set-cookie (trusted-set-cookie), set-cookie-reload, remove-cookie, set-local-storage-item, set-session-storage-item (trusted- forms), remove-local-storage-item, remove-session-storage-itemdom_ops.odin: operations on the document, fed by the mutation journal: the nodes inserted since the last pass are looked at once (never the whole document again, unless the journal lost entries), before the page styles, before every script that is about to run, and when the parser finishes. An inline script's text is rewritten before it runs (before_script). Cookies and storage are written through the page's own cookie jar and storage manager. Behavior as uBlock Origin's: asap, stay, a plain operation rests once the parse is done; text operations and clicks watch (clicks up to 10 s). Regular expressions are JavaScript's (jsre.odin: captures, lazy quantifiers, look-around, back-references, a step budget).
network (Odin, in the loader)json-prune-fetch-response (jpfr), json-prune-xhr-response (jpxhr), xml-prune, trusted-replace-fetch-response, trusted-replace-xhr-response (replace-in-response), and the filter option $replace=rewrite.odin: a fetch.Body_Filter on the response, by URL (and method), before the page reads it. JSON and XML answers are held until complete and rewritten once (JSON pruned by path with wildcards, XML by element selector, text by regular expression); nothing is held or parsed for a request no rule targets. Content-Length is dropped and the HTTP cache keeps the server's version.
network, in the markupset-constant and json-prune of a variable the page's own HTML assigns (var ytInitialPlayerResponse = {...})the same Body_Filter on the document: the literal is found in the stream, pruned (or its property set) and written back before the parser reads it; the rest of the page flows through. A set-constant ... undefined on ytInitialPlayerResponse.<key> also prunes <key> from the answers of /youtubei/v1/player (the same object, asked for by the page for the next video), before any $replace= / trusted-replace-* filter of the list.
engine hooks (C in the engine, no interpreted code)set-constant (set, trusted-set-constant), abort-on-property-read (aopr), abort-on-property-write (aopw), abort-current-script (acs, acis), abort-on-stack-trace (aost), no-setTimeout-if (nostif), no-setInterval-if (nosiif), nano-setTimeout-booster, nano-setInterval-booster, no-fetch-if, no-xhr-if, addEventListener-defuser (aeld), window.open-defuser (nowoif), noeval, nowebrtc, json-prune (jp, on JSON.parse)native/js/engine/qjs_blocker.c: before the first script the browser hands the rules to the engine (wj_hook_install), which installs C accessors and replaced functions; the decision (function text, current script, stack, arguments, URL) is made in C with the page's values, patterns are real JavaScript regular expressions. A call a rule does not concern costs the check and the call of the original.
JavaScript (last resort)raw #%# JavaScript rules; every hook scriptlet when blocker.hooks.native is offscriptlets.js run in the realm. Off by default for everything but the raw rules, which are the user's own code.
accepted, no effectjson-edit and spoof-css families, addEventListener-loggeruBlock Origin's logging and experimental ones: the line is understood and does nothing.

Count of scriptlets that still run as JavaScript with the default settings: none, besides the lines the user wrote as raw JavaScript.

The arguments of trusted-replace-*-response follow uBlock Origin's: the third one is url:<pattern> method:<verb>, or a bare pattern (text or /regex/, colons and spaces allowed) that is the URL's. trusted-rpfr / trusted-rpxhr are aliases. The url: form is also read by json-prune-*-response and xml-prune.

#The first pages of a session

While the real filter index is not there (no valid cache in the profile: first start, a format change, lists changed on disk), only the small base list is in force and the lists are compiled on a thread. A request let through meanwhile would escape every rule of the lists: the first page of the session would carry its ad data (a YouTube watch page: ytInitialPlayerResponse.adPlacements intact). So the loader parks the requests to the network (fetch.hold_requests) from the start until the compile job is done, for at most 20 s (BOOT_HOLD_MS), then starts them in order through the real rules. With a valid cache the index is loaded in a few milliseconds at start and nothing is held. about:, data: and file: are never held.

Stand-ins for $redirect: noop.js, noop.css, noop.html / noopframe, noop.txt, empty, 1x1.gif, 2x2.png, 3x2.png, 32x32.png (generated), noopmp3-0.1s, noopmp4-1s, google-analytics.com/ga.js, analytics.js, inpage_linkid.js, googletagmanager.com/gtm.js, googletagservices.com/gpt.js, googlesyndication.com/adsbygoogle.js, scorecardresearch.com/beacon.js, amazon_apstag.js, doubleclick.net/instream/ad_status.js, nobab.js, chartbeat.js, outbrain-widget.js (and uBO's aliases).

#Interface

  • The icon at the end of the address row: green (filtering), amber (only the built-in list yet), grey (off, or off for this site, or not applicable), with a badge of the page's blocked requests; the tooltip says N blocked on this page (M in all). It costs nothing at rest.
  • The panel: power switch of the site (a click reloads), counters, graph of the blocks over the page's load, switches (element hiding, scriptlets, remote fonts, large media, hard mode), the matrix of the page's hosts by request type (a click on a cell blocks, allows, then resets that host and type for this site; Shift+click for every site), the element picker, the log, the dashboard, reload.
  • The element picker (panel, context menu "Block element…"): aim, click, a precision slider walks the candidate selectors from the most to the least specific, the selector is editable, matches are outlined, Preview hides them for real, Create adds site##selector to My filters.
  • about:blocker: Settings, Filter lists, My filters, My rules, Whitelist, Journal, Statistics, About. The whole configuration (lists, rules, sites, filters) exports and imports as one text file.
  • Context menu of the page: Block element…, Block this resource. About:config: blocker.*.

#Preferences (about:config, blocker.*)

enabled, cosmetic.enabled, scriptlets.enabled, html_filters.enabled, html_filters.max_body, popup.enabled, collapse.enabled, redirects.enabled, removeparam.enabled, update.enabled, update.interval_hours, update.start_delay_s, update.max_list_bytes, log.capacity, log.always, large_media_kb, hard_mode, remote_fonts, cosmetic.debounce_ms, cosmetic.max_selectors, engine.cache, badge.enabled, console.enabled, matrix.max_hosts, graph.points.

#Measuring

  • build\adblockbench.exe <lists dir> (src/tools/adblockbench): compile time, load time, memory, requests per second, latency distribution on real lists.
  • tools\blocker_perf.ps1: loads each site with and without the blocker in the real browser (a fresh copy of a profile that has the lists, a cold HTTP cache) and collects WREN_LOAD_REPORT lines (first paint, readyState complete, requests, blocked, bytes, DOM nodes, CPU time, memory). WREN_BLOCKER_TRACE=<file> logs what the page hooks cost.
  • src/tools/blockerpages: the same in the headless stack.
  • tools\blocker_js.ps1: how much JavaScript the interpreter runs for a page (WREN_JS_PROFILE samples summed over the tab's pages, and those of the blocker's own scripts), two executables side by side and the page without the blocker.
  • WREN_HOOKBENCH=1 build\blockertest.exe: what a hooked API costs per call (ns), without the blocker, with the native hooks, with the JavaScript versions.
  • Unit tests: odin test src/adblock, odin test src/blocker; end to end: blockertest (tools\test_all.ps1).

#Results

Engine (real lists: EasyList, EasyPrivacy, uBlock filters, AdGuard Base, Peter Lowe, URLhaus; 182,000 network and 73,000 cosmetic filters): compile 290 ms, index 24 MB, cold load 13 ms, a request in about 4 us (p50 3 us, p99 21 us; 26 us before the gram index and the regex prefilter).

Blocking changes the order in which a page's JavaScript runs. When a blocked script is what kept a heavy page script waiting, that script starts earlier and can hold the main thread before the first frame (CNN with cdn.optimizely.com, Daily Mail's ad loader): the first paint is then later although the bytes, requests and CPU time fell. An exception for optimizely.com brought CNN's first paint back to 1.0 s. Where little is blocked (the Guardian's blocked requests are beacons, Fox News served none from the lists) the numbers are the same within noise.

#Scriptlets without JavaScript

The interpreter's work for a page (tools\blocker_js.ps1: the samples WREN_JS_PROFILE takes of the page's functions, summed over every page of the tab, 20 to 25 s after the navigation; a profile with the lists; before is the build that ran the scriptlets as JavaScript, after this one). The samples of the blocker's own scripts (wren-blocker:...) are 0 in both builds on these sites.

sitebeforeafterblocker off
theguardian.com159146156
allrecipes.com10599269
weather.com5565421144
dailymail.co.uk112511191119
edition.cnn.com1212229
youtube.com (watch), median of 4170517331240

Reading: the scriptlets add nothing to the interpreter's work (before and after are the same within the noise of a sample taken every few thousand interrupt checks), and where the blocker removes scripts the page's work falls (allrecipes, weather.com, CNN). What the table cannot show is that the blocker no longer has a script in the realm at all: with the default settings no JavaScript of the blocker is compiled or run (the page's wren-blocker:scriptlets script exists only for raw #%# rules, or with blocker.hooks.native off). On YouTube the page itself does more work with the blocker on than off (about 40 %): it reacts to what is blocked, which is not the blocker's own work.

What a hooked API costs per call (WREN_HOOKBENCH=1, median of 3 runs, ns per iteration of a loop that itself costs about 35):

callno blockernative hooksJavaScript versions
setTimeout + clearTimeout, rule on the function's text138019253816
JSON.parse of a small object, a json-prune rule375331958415
read of a property a set-constant defines5677 (a miss on the window)118177

A rule with a text pattern has to read the callback's source (about 0.5 us); a rule with an empty pattern does not.
